name: Mohammadhossein Amouei
intro: I study how machine learning can help us understand and secure software when source code is unavailable.
bio: I am a PhD candidate at McGill University, supervised by Prof. Benjamin C. M. Fung. My research brings together software reverse engineering, natural language processing, and representation learning.

I focus on binary code similarity: identifying related functions across compilers, optimization settings, and architectures. My broader interests include language models for code and learning-guided vulnerability discovery.

research.title: AI for Cybersecurity
research.text: Developing machine learning and language-model-based methods to understand software behavior and support security analysis.
research.tags: Machine learning · Language models · Software security

research.title: Program Analysis and Reverse Engineering
research.text: Analyzing source code and binaries to recover program semantics and identify related code across compilers, optimization settings, and architectures.
research.tags: Binary analysis · Program understanding · Code similarity

research.title: Automated Vulnerability Detection
research.text: Detecting vulnerabilities in source code and binaries through program analysis, learned representations, and code similarity.

research.title: Software Supply Chain Security
research.text: Investigating code provenance, third-party dependencies, and the propagation of known vulnerabilities across reused software components.
research.tags: Code provenance · Dependency analysis · Software reuse
